text: We couldn't find a surf school with its own website confirming lessons at Eastbourne. Buzz Active, on Royal Parade, teaches paddleboarding, windsurfing, sailing and kayaking, but its tourism listing doesn't mention surfing. If you want a surf lesson in Sussex, Brighton Watersports runs mobile lessons, mostly at Shoreham, with wetsuits included.

Eastbourne faces south-east into the Channel, and surf here depends on passing swell and wind. As we couldn't confirm lifeguard cover or hazards from the council or RNLI, don't head out alone if you're new. Learn with a school first, and check conditions and safety signs on the day.

text: With small, occasional Channel waves, a large foam board or a longboard gives you the best chance of catching something. Water on the Sussex coast runs from about 6 to 8°C in late winter to 17 to 19°C in late summer, according to Wittering Surf Shop. On flat days, Buzz Active on Royal Parade offers paddleboarding courses.

cards.text: Wittering Surf Shop, further west on the same coast, suggests a 3/2 or shorty July to October, 4/3 in May, June and November, and 5/4 with boots and gloves December to April.
